rule.description: The shared BIO method contract (the struct behind BIO_METHOD) requires readiness handler slots from every BIO implementation, so every statically declared method table and every dynamically built method is dragged into a capability that only some resources can provide.

checks.description: Detect readiness handler slots declared on the shared BIO method contract, beyond the classic BIO method operations (type, name, bwrite, bread, bputs, bgets, ctrl, create, destroy, callback_ctrl).
checks.detected_relation: bio_method_st -> readiness capability required from every BIO implementation
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A capability that only some resources can provide is welded into the one interface that every BIO implementation must instantiate, instead of being an opt-in extension of that interface.

matches.evidence: The shared method struct declares a non-blocking-mode toggle handler that every method table must carry.
The shared method struct declares a poll-based read-wait handler that every method table must carry.
The shared method struct declares a poll-based write-wait handler that every method table must carry.

checks.description: Detect statically declared bio_method_st tables whose initializer supplies any of the readiness slots, i.e. implementations dragged into the capability by the shared contract.
checks.detected_relation: BIO method table -> readiness slots supplied through the shared method contract
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Memory buffers, null sinks, stdio streams, the BIO pair and forwarding filters cannot genuinely provide kernel readiness, yet the shared contract forces them to fill the slots and invent answers.

matches.evidence: Memory-buffer method table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots for a resource that never blocks.
Null-sink method table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots for a resource that never blocks.
Stdio method table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots although stdio streams expose no readiness signal.
Socket method table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots through the shared contract.
File-descriptor method table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots through the shared contract.
Datagram method table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots through the shared contract.
Connect method table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots through the shared contract.
Accept method table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots through the shared contract.
Pre-connected-pair method table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots for an in-memory pipe.
Buffering filter table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots it can only forward to the next BIO.
Null filter table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots it can only forward to the next BIO.
Non-blocking placement filter table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots it can only forward to the next BIO.
Cipher filter table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots it can only forward to the next BIO.
Base64 filter table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots it can only forward to the next BIO.
Digest filter table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots it can only forward to the next BIO.
ASN.1 stream table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots it can only forward to the next BIO.
SSL record-layer table supplies set_nbio, wait_readable and wait_writeable slots through the shared contract.

checks.description: Detect readiness hooks installed into a dynamically built BIO method through the BIO_meth_set_* extension accessors.
checks.detected_relation: dynamically constructed BIO method -> readiness capability mandated by the extension surface
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The accessor surface makes the same capability a build-time requirement for runtime-constructed methods: a method composed from the public accessors cannot exist without answering the readiness slots.

matches.evidence: The libtls callback method is coerced through an extension accessor to install a non-blocking-mode handler.
The libtls callback method is coerced through an extension accessor to install a read-wait handler.
The libtls callback method is coerced through an extension accessor to install a write-wait handler.

excluded.candidate: test-only BIO method tables under tests/ (regression suites)
excluded.reason: Not production code; the rule analyzes the 18 production method-table sources only.

excluded.candidate: the classic BIO method operations (type, name, bwrite, bread, bputs, bgets, ctrl, create, destroy, callback_ctrl)
excluded.reason: Part of the long-standing BIO contract; the rule flags only function-pointer members beyond them.

excluded.candidate: the accessor implementations and prototypes in bio_meth.c/include/openssl/bio.h themselves
excluded.reason: They define the extension surface; the rule reports the interface members, the forced tables and the dynamic installation sites, not accessor plumbing.
